questions.topic: A country that writes no sharp s at all
questions.learningObjective: Identify Switzerland as the no-ß country

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

answer.exemplar: Switzerland drops the sharp s entirely, so a street is spelled Strasse with ss. Germany and Austria keep Straße with ß, which would be wrong in a Swiss text.

questions.explanation: Swiss orthography forbids ß and writes ss, so Strasse is correct. The key value is Switzerland drops the sharp s entirely, so a street is spelled Strasse with ss. Germany and Austria keep Straße with ß, which would be wrong in a Swiss text..

questions.explanation: Austrian usage is masculine, giving der, while German standard usage is neuter, giving das. The key is C, "der in Austria and das in Germany". Option D ("der in both countries") is wrong: treats "der in both countries" as if it followed from the evidence.
